evals.name: psychrometric-rust
evals.prompt: Calculate the enthalpy, dew point, and specific volume of air at 25°C dry-bulb, 50% RH, at sea level. Then write a Rust function that takes (T_db, RH, P) and returns a struct with all derived psychrometric properties. Include unit tests that validate against the known values you just computed.
evals.expected_output: Correct thermodynamic values at 25°C/50%RH/101325Pa, a Rust struct with psychrometric calculations, and unit tests validating the computed values.

assertions.name: specific_volume_correct
assertions.description: Specific volume at 25°C/50%RH is approximately 0.858 m³/kg_da (within 2%)

assertions.name: rust_struct_provided
assertions.description: Output includes a Rust struct with multiple psychrometric fields (not just one value)

assertions.name: unit_tests_present
assertions.description: Rust code includes #[test] functions that validate against computed reference values

assertions.name: physics_constraints
assertions.description: Tests validate physical constraints: dew point < dry bulb, positive enthalpy increment over 0°C baseline

assertions.name: ashrae_citation
assertions.description: References ASHRAE Handbook of Fundamentals or Hyland-Wexler correlations for saturation pressure

evals.name: ashrae-62-1-vrp
evals.prompt: I need the minimum outdoor air rate for a 3,000 sq ft conference room with a default occupant density per ASHRAE 62.1-2022. Give me the table citation, the VRP math, and a Python function that computes V_oz for any zone given area, population, and zone category.
evals.expected_output: ASHRAE 62.1 table citation, VRP formula breakdown with actual numbers for the conference room, and a Python function with type hints that generalizes the calculation.

assertions.name: table_citation_present
assertions.description: Cites the specific ASHRAE 62.1 table for occupancy category rates (Table 6.2.2.1 or equivalent)

assertions.name: vrp_formula_shown
assertions.description: Shows V_bz = Rp × Pz + Ra × Az (or equivalent ventilation rate procedure equation)

assertions.name: conference_room_result
assertions.description: Computes ~930 cfm for the 3000 sq ft conference room (accounts for 150 people at default density)

assertions.name: python_function_generalized
assertions.description: Python function accepts arbitrary area, population, and zone category — not hardcoded to conference rooms

assertions.name: ez_accounted_for
assertions.description: Explains or parameterizes zone air distribution effectiveness (Ez) in the V_oz calculation

assertions.name: default_density_correct
assertions.description: Uses correct default occupant density for conference rooms (50 per 1000 sq ft per 62.1)

evals.name: openstudio-vav-measure
evals.prompt: Write an OpenStudio measure that replaces all constant-volume terminal boxes in a model with VAV terminals, applying a minimum airflow fraction of 0.3. Then write a Python script that parses the EnergyPlus SQL output and compares zone airflow rates before and after the measure to confirm the VAV boxes are operating correctly.
evals.expected_output: A complete Ruby OpenStudio measure with argument handling and model manipulation logic, plus a Python SQL parsing script that queries and compares airflow data.

assertions.name: ruby_measure_complete
assertions.description: Ruby file includes name, description, arguments, and run methods following OpenStudio ModelMeasure pattern

assertions.name: cv_to_vav_conversion
assertions.description: Correctly identifies AirTerminal:SingleDuct:Uncontrolled (or ConstantVolume) and creates VAV replacements

assertions.name: min_airflow_fraction
assertions.description: Sets minimum airflow fraction to 0.3 (or makes it a configurable argument with 0.3 default)

assertions.name: python_sql_parser
assertions.description: Python script connects to EnergyPlus SQLite database and queries airflow-related tables

assertions.name: before_after_comparison
assertions.description: Script compares airflow rates between baseline and post-measure runs

assertions.name: error_handling_ruby
assertions.description: Ruby measure uses registerError/registerWarning/registerInfo properly with graceful failure
